title: Fluctuation-Induced Bistability in the Dissipative Dynamics of Generic Cavity-Matter Quantum Systems
authors: Luisa Tolle, Simon B. Jäger, Ameneh Sheikhan, Corinna Kollath, Catalin-Mihai Halati
abstract: We demonstrate that fluctuation-induced bistability is a robust and generic phenomenon in strongly interacting many-body systems with strong light-matter coupling. We identify a common microscopic mechanism based on resonances between photonic transitions and many-body energy scales, unifying the emergence of fluctuation-induced bistability across a broad class of models, including interacting spins, fermions, and bosons coupled to cavity modes. We develop complementary methods to study both the steady-state properties of fluctuation-induced bistability and its dynamical formation at finite times. In particular, we introduce the dressed-state rate equation approach, which reveals rich metastable dynamics and enables the investigation of its system-size dependence. By comparing its predictions with numerically-exact tensor-network simulations, we identify signatures of fluctuation-induced bistability already in small systems on finite timescales. Our results establish fluctuation-induced bistability as a universal feature of dissipative cavity-coupled many-body systems and provide a general framework for the investigation of its non-equilibrium dynamics across a wide range of hybrid quantum platforms.
summary: This paper establishes that fluctuation-induced bistability is a universal feature of dissipative cavity-coupled many-body systems. The authors use advanced rate equation methods (DSRE) and compare them with tensor network simulations to map out the non-equilibrium dynamics. It provides a general theoretical tool for analyzing complex quantum phenomena in hybrid light-matter platforms.
main_problem: The paper investigates fluctuation-induced bistability, demonstrating that this phenomenon is a robust and generic feature in strongly interacting many-body systems coupled to dissipative cavities.
main_result: Bistability is shown to be universal across various models (spins, fermions, bosons) due to resonances between photon transitions and many-body energy scales. The dynamics are studied using advanced rate equation approaches that capture non-equilibrium behavior.
method: The authors employ complementary theoretical frameworks, including the Dressed-State Rate Equation (DSRE) approach derived via Mori-Zwanzig formalism, and compare results with numerically exact tensor-network simulations (tMPS).
model_or_system: The system models generic cavity-matter quantum interactions, encompassing interacting spins (XX model), fermions (Fermi-Hubbard), and bosons (Bose-Hubbard) coupled to a dissipative photonic mode governed by a Lindblad master equation.
key_observables: Probability distribution $p(	heta)$ of the imbalance $	heta$, steady-state properties, and time evolution of observables like $\langle	heta^2angle$ and coherence ($C_2$).
important_parameters: Strong coupling regime ($U/J, \hbar g/J \gg 1$), system size dependence (bistability emerges for large $L$), and local Hilbert-space cutoff ($N_{\max}$).
main_assumptions: The DSRE approach involves approximations like neglecting coherences between degenerate eigenstates or truncating the hierarchy of equations; MF+fluct. assumes rapid thermalization.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $p(	heta)$ for different systems and cutoffs, showing bistability regions. Other figures track time evolution of observables ($\langle	heta^2angle$, etc.) using tMPS, confirming slow dynamics in the bistable regime.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem by defining the Hamiltonian and master equation. It then develops and applies the DSRE method to analyze steady-state properties and show the universality of bistability across different particle types. Finally, it validates these findings by comparing results with tMPS simulations tracking non-equilibrium time evolution.
why_interesting: This work provides a general theoretical framework for understanding emergent non-linear dynamics (bistability) in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant to cavity QED and superconducting circuit research where dissipation plays a crucial role.
